subject: Pricing & committed-use discount — follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Johnson <alice@acme.ai>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 08 May 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pricing & committed-use discount — follow-up

Hi Alice — great to meet today. Thanks for taking the time to walk through Acme's planned product flows and token profiles. Quick recap (so we're aligned) and a couple of asks so I can pull together precise pricing: 

- Usage profile: you said production inference ~120M tokens/mo today, with peak batch jobs and dev/test adding another ~30M; target ramp to ~400M/mo by end of Year 2.
- Model mix: majority LLM text-generation for chat (approx 70%), smaller embedding/semantic search footprint (30%).
- Budget/Target economics: you mentioned a target unit cost in the ballpark of $60–$80 per 1M tokens (goal to keep total monthly spend within your engineering budget).
- Contract interest: startup program (credit + intro pricing) and a committed-use option (12–24 months) to get a deeper discount.

Next steps I proposed on the call:
1) You confirm an expected monthly tokens range (low / expected / high) so I can model committed tiers.
2) I'll share two proposals: a startup program path (12 months of credits + standard pricing) and a committed-use path with tiered discounts and ramping commitments.
3) Procurement: if committed discount is attractive, we can loop in procurement for SOW / signature — happy to coordinate timelines.

I've attached a quick token model I asked our solutions team to start (Estimated_token_modeling.xlsx) and a short explainer on our startup program (startup-program-terms.pdf). If you can reply with a simple low/expected/high tokens per month, I'll run numbers and propose a couple of concrete $/1M token targets.

Thanks — Marissa

Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0123

Attachments: Estimated_token_modeling.xlsx, startup-program-terms.pdf

From: Alice Johnson <alice@acme.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acme AI Procurement <procurement@acme.ai>
Date: Fri, 08 May 2026 16:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pricing & committed-use discount — follow-up

Marissa — thanks for the recap and the docs. Confirming numbers from our side (low / expected / high monthly tokens):
- Low: 80M/month (pilot + early prod)
- Expected: 150M/month (steady state Y1 average)
- High: 400M/month (full ramp by end of Y2)

Budget: our current engineering allocation for LLM infra is roughly $8k–$15k/month in Year 1, with potential to increase if unit economics justify it. That maps to an implied target of about $50–$100 per 1M tokens (we've been using $75/1M as an internal planning number).

We are definitely interested in committed-use pricing if Redwood can offer a multi-year incentive (2-year) with predictable unit pricing and a ramp schedule. Also curious how startup program credits would combine with committed discounts (if at all).

Procurement is CC'd — they prefer to see a clear committed-tier proposal (tokens/month + effective $/1M + termination/true-up language) before drafting internal paperwork. Happy to hop on a 30-min procurement call next week.

Best,
Alice Johnson
Head of Product | Acme AI
alice@acme.ai

On Fri, May 8, 2026 at 2:12 PM Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Hi Alice — great to meet today. Thanks for taking the time to walk through Acme's planned product flows and token profiles. Quick recap ...

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Johnson <alice@acme.ai>, Acme AI Procurement <procurement@acme.ai>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 10 May 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pricing & committed-use discount — follow-up

Hi Alice / team — thanks for the detail, really helpful. Based on the low/expected/high you provided, I ran a quick set of options for you (high-level):

Option A — Startup program (no commit):
- 12 months of credits equal to $50k applied over first 12 months (effectively reduces Yr1 cash out).
- Standard pay-as-you-go pricing after credits; typical $/1M by model class will be higher than committed tiers.
- Good if you want to conserve cash and experiment early.

Option B — 12-month committed-use (ramp)
- Commit to a ramp of 120M -> 200M -> 300M tokens/mo over 12 months (example), with an average commit of ~207M/mo.
- Discount: 10% off list across committed usage; additional 3% if Allen-MAC true-up cadence (quarterly).
- Early termination: pro-rated true-up + 60-day notice.

Option C — 24-month committed (best unit economics)
- Commit to a two-year ramp with Year1 expected 150M/mo average and Year2 350M/mo average.
- Discount: 15% off list for committed usage; 5% additional incentive if you sign a 24-month agreement within 30 days.
- Includes a one-time onboarding credit of $25k and a 90-day discounted trial period for non-production traffic.

Preliminary $/1M examples (effective) using Option C and your expected 150M/mo baseline:  
- List (model-weighted) effective: $95 per 1M tokens
- After 15% committed discount: ~$80.75 per 1M tokens
- If we apply the 5% sign-by incentive: ~$76.71 per 1M tokens

Notes:
- Startup credits do not stack with committed discounts on the committed-portion; credits apply to non-committed usage and onboarding fees. We can discuss limited stacking in special cases.
- I'll attach a simple committed-use tiers workbook (Committed_Use_Tiers_v3.xlsx) that shows the math for your low/expected/high scenarios.

Next steps I propose:
1) Marissa to update the workbook with your preferred ramp numbers (low/expected/high per month) and produce a two-sided proposal (startup path vs 24-month committed).
2) Procurement to confirm any non-standard contract terms they require (SLAs, audit language, data residency).
3) Schedule a procurement + legal sync (30 min) next week — I have availability Tue/Thu mornings PST.

If that looks good I can put together a draft term sheet with exact $/1M numbers and cadence for true-ups.

Thanks — Marissa

Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0123

Attachments: Committed_Use_Tiers_v3.xlsx

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Pricing & committed-use discount — follow-up

FYI — forwarding the thread with Acme. They gave low/expected/high (80 / 150 / 400M tokens) and are targeting ~$75/1M as their internal planning number. Procurement wants a clear committed-tier proposal.

Proposed internal ask: can we offer a 15% committed discount for a 24-month deal with a one-time $25k onboarding credit (Option C above)? I sketched effective $/1M of ~$76.7 on their 150M baseline which is close to their target. Want to understand commercial guardrails (min desk, early termination language) and whether we can extend the 5% sign-by incentive.

Also: capacity check — their peak pattern would be ~400M/mo by Year2; we should confirm whether we need to reserve Dedicated capacity or if hosted burst will cover. Dylan — can you confirm throughput and any recommended routing/quantization options that would help lower unit cost if needed? Vivek — want to confirm whether we should approve 15% + $25k credit (with standard early termination/true-up) or push for 10%/12mo as a fallback.

Thanks — Marissa
